newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH KOMERCNI RESULTS FALL BELOW EXPECTATIONS.
newsitem.headline: CZECH KOMERCNI RESULTS FALL BELOW EXPECTATIONS.

text.p: Komercni Banka a.s. , the largest Czech commercial bank, on Thursday posted first half 1997 net profits which fell well below most analysts' expectations.

Komercni said that its net profits, to internatonal accounting standards, dropped to 1.64 billion crowns from 2.53 billion in the same period in 1996. A Reuters survey of analysts on Wednesday had predicted the bank's net profit at between 1.8 and 2.4 billion crowns.
"It's a surprise and the results are really disappointing," said Miroslav Nosal of Patria Finance.
Nosal said Komercni's results had probably been influenced by the crown crisis in May and June when the central bank hiked interest rates in a vain attempt to defend the Czech currency.

During the crisis, interbank overnight rates surged to over 100 percent from around 12 percent. The Lombard rate was raised to 50 percent from 14 percent -- it has since been cut to 23 percent -- and the discount rate remains at 13.0 percent from 10.5 before the crisis began.
Komercni put a brave face on the figures saying the results testified "to sustained growth potential."

It added in a statement: "Negative external conditions - the overall slowdown of the Czech economy with a number of adverse consequences, strong currency shudders in May and June followed by turbulences on the interbank market - have impeded but not stopped the dynamics of growth."
As evidence, Komercni said that its volume of client loans increased by 5.1 percent to 252.4 billion crowns.

It also said that assets rose to 456.2 billion crowns, an increase of 2.3 percent from the end of 1996 and that costs and expenses had been cut with a reduction in staff of 937 employees to a total of 14,903.
However, it admitted that total "other income" on its balance sheet fell by 96 percent to 101 million crowns.

The main impetus for this fall was its unrealised gains and losses on securities which were -1.15 billion crowns compared with a 444 million crown gain in the first six months of 1996. The change represents a 359 perecnt fall from 1996.
Komercni also raised the share of loans under "special review" as a proportion of total loans to 26.13 percent from 25.61 perecent at the end of 1996.

"This is primarily due to delays in the enactment of legislation relating to debt recovery and to the impact of negative financial factors and of the currency crisis on KB clients," Komercni's statement accompanying the results said.
Komercni's share price has fallen sharply since the beginning of the year, underperforming a falling PX50 index by 24 percent and declining in absolute terms by 28 percent.

At Thursday's fixing, Komercni fell 49 crowns to 1,611 but John Vax, director of capital markets it ING Barings, said the issue may already have fallen sharply enough not to be too adversely affected by the first half results.

"The price has come down quite a bit over the last weeks in expectation of poor performance due to the (crown) crisis and the general poor economic performance. So maybe the shares are already fairly valued," he said.
